comments.story_title: Why is Git better than Subversion?
comments.why_zh: Linus 谈为什么 SVN 不值得在其上构建
comments.quote_zh: 他提到自己没有选择 SVN 的原因
comments.text_zh: 在 Linus Torvalds 于 Google 做的关于 git 的演讲[0]中，他提到自己没有选择 SVN 的原因（这也是他认为除了构建 GIT 别无选择的原因之一）是，SVN 的使命宣言写的是“To create a compelling replacement for CVS”……而 Linus 对此深恶痛绝，因此无法理解自己为什么还要用一个“有说服力的替代品”来替代它。有趣的是，在与两位 SVN 开发者一起的《Open Source projects and poisonous people》演讲[1]中，他们提到自己是特意选择那句话的，就是为了确保每个人对项目范围有共识——在人们熟悉和习惯的东西上改进，而不是搞狂野的新东西。具体来说，是因为经常有人带着一些宏大的计划进入社区，而那些计划只会让项目范围爆炸。当然，这在多大程度上能算一条普遍规则可以争论，但在这个例子里，GIT 就是从根本上、而且显而易见地比 SVN 更好的选择。如果有人试图把 SVN 变成 GIT，那只会直接杀死 SVN，所以把它做成一个新项目才是正确的做法。SVN 从其设计上就注定要死。看到如今 GIT 的采用率（尤其是因为 GitHub 这样的工具），对喜欢认为有时候重新开始是唯一选择的人来说，非常鼓舞人心。当然，你想构建的东西确实必须比你试图取代的旧东西好上那么多。所以我同意你——可以这么说
comments.text: In Linus Torvalds' talk on git at google[0], he mentions that the reason why he did not choose SVN (one of the reasons why he saw no other way but to build GIT) was that SVNs mission statement read "To create a compelling replacement for CVS"... which Linus hated with a passion and thus could not see why he would even use "a compelling replacement" of. Interestingly enough, in the 'Open Source projects and poisonous people' talk[1] with two SVN developers, they mention how they chose that line specifically to make sure that everybody is on the same page with the scope of the project - improving upon what people knew and were used to instead of wild, new things. Specifically because they would often have people come into the community with some grand plans that would have just exploded the scope. It is of course arguable to what extent there could be a general rule to this, but in this case, GIT is just so fundamentally and obviously the better option than SVN. Had somebody tried to make SVN into GIT, it would have simply killed SVN, so it was the right course of action to make it a new project. SVN was destined to die by its design. To see the GIT adoption rates these days (particularly due to tools like GitHub) is very encouraging to people who like to think that sometimes, starting over fresh is the only option. Of course, the thing you want to build really has to be that much better than the old thing you're trying to replace. So I agree with you - it's alright to say that

comments.why_zh: Linus 称所有非分布式版本控制系统无用
comments.quote_zh: 他把所有非分布式版本控制系统称为无用
comments.text_zh: 这篇文章勾起了回忆。早在 2007 年，我刚看过 Linus 在 Google 关于 Git 的演讲（[VIDEO]），他在里面把所有非分布式版本控制系统都称为无用。从他那场演讲里我完全没搞懂 DVCS。我试着玩了玩 Git，结果因为糟糕的 CLI 极其沮丧。我以为 Git 也许只是一阵风潮。但后来越来越多的人一直在说它有多棒。这是让 Git 终于在我这里开窍的文章之一。关键引文：不需要花哨的 metadata、重命名跟踪等等。你唯一需要存储的是每次变更前后 tree 的状态。哪些文件被重命名？哪些被复制？哪些被删除？哪些行被添加？哪些被删除？哪些行内部发生了修改？哪些文本块被从一个文件复制到另一个文件？你不应该需要关心这些问题中的任何一个，当然也不应该需要保留特殊的跟踪数据来帮你回答它们：对 tree 的所有变更（新增、删除、重命名、编辑等）都隐式编码在 tree 两个状态之间的 delta 里；你只需跟踪内容是什么。我用 Git 已经 7 年了，无法想象自己以前怎么能用那些不作用于整棵 tree 的版本控制。
comments.text: This article brings back memories. Back in 2007, I had just watched Linus' presentation on Git at Google ( [VIDEO] ) where he called all non distributed version control systems as useless. I could not make any sense of the DVCS from his talk. I tried to play with Git and it was extremely frustrating due to the poor CLI. I thought may be Git is just a fad. But then more and more people kept talking about how awesome it is. This was one of the article where Git finally clicked for me. The key quote: There is no need for fancy metadata, rename tracking and so forth. The only thing you need to store is the state of the tree before and after each change. What files were renamed? Which ones were copied? Which ones were deleted? What lines were added? Which ones were removed? Which lines had changes made inside them? Which slabs of text were copied from one file to another? You shouldn't have to care about any of these questions and you certainly shouldn't have to keep special tracking data in order to help you answer them: all the changes to the tree (additions, deletes, renames, edits etc) are implicitly encoded in the delta between the two states of the tree; you just track what is the content. It's been 7 years since I have been using Git and I can't imagine how I ever worked with version control which didn't work on the entire tree.

comments.text_zh: 我只有一个关于 Linus 的故事。早在 2007 年，他本来要来做一个关于 git 的演讲。我得在演讲前紧接着对一位候选人做现场面试，但我还是设法搞定，及时赶到，正好看到演讲开始。我从没见过他本人，觉得可能挺有意思，尤其是因为在那之前我确实在一些项目里用过 git。这场演讲后来被录了下来，网上在这里：[VIDEO] 我觉得自己撑了十分钟，觉得实在受不了就走了。那种能量周围已经够多了，没必要还心甘情愿坐在那儿多吸收一些。再说，我还有面试要整理成文。
comments.text: I only have one Linus story. Way back in 2007, he was supposed to come and give a talk on git. I had to do an on-site interview with a candidate immediately beforehand, but managed to get it done and got there in time to see the talk start. I had never seen him in person and figured it might be interesting, particularly since I had actually used git on some projects prior to that point. This wound up being recorded, and it's online here: [VIDEO] I think I lasted ten minutes and left after deciding it was too much. There was enough of that kind of energy going around already to willingly sit there and take in more. Besides, I had an interview to write up.
